title: Publish account lifecycle events for provisioning and billing
description:
Feature: Products learn about account changes without polling
  Scenario: An operator grants a Papyrus site to an account
    Given an entitlement change committed to the account document
    When the change is published
    Then exactly one event {type: entitlement.changed, accountId, product, status, revision, operationId, at} reaches that product's subscriber
    And the event names no person by email and carries no token

  Scenario: Delivery fails
    When the subscriber is down
    Then the event is retried and can be replayed from a durable source, and consumers apply events idempotently by operationId

Event types: account.created, entitlement.changed, membership.changed.
Consumers: Papyrus provisions or suspends a newsroom tenant on entitlement.changed; billing (kanbus-a78bcd) opens or ends billing lines from the same events.
Open design for Ryan:
- the transport (EventBridge bus with a rule per product, or SQS per product);
- whether events are derived from the account audit or written by the commit itself;
- the delivery guarantee.
Canonical data stays the account files in S3; any queue or catalog is supplemental.

comments.author: home
comments.text: 2026-10-31 (Billing planner): the billing plan (kanbus-a78bcdbc) treats these events as prompts, not triggers: on entitlement.changed to active with no billing line, billing opens an operator follow-up to attach a plan (kanbus-8e3174); on disabled, a follow-up to end the line. Automatic line creation from events would charge a client without an operator choosing a plan and price, so it is an open question for Ryan in the billing epic. Consumer idempotency by operationId matches the billing journal design.
